To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tax subsidy to employer-paid health premiums is not an effective way to provide health insurance to low- and moderate-income families.
(a) the tax expenditure for health insurance is a large one, and (b) it is regressive.

1) the tax subsidy for employer-paid premiums for health insurance is a large and growing tax expenditure, with the largest share going to the highest income taxpayers and 2) the tax subsidy is a major factor in explaining the growth of the health care sector and in the rising health care costs borne by the government and private sector.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of tax expenditures on employer-paid health insurance.
the impact of tax expenditures on the cost of health insurance and with the implications of tax expenditures for the cost of health care.

the effects on health insurance coverage and costs of the following policy options: (a) increasing the cost of coverage by reducing the value of employer-paid premiums; (b) reducing the value of coverage by reducing employer-paid premiums; and (c) reducing the value and cost of coverage by increasing the cost-sharing provisions of health insurance plans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tax treatment of employer-provided health insurance is a major factor in the high and rapidly rising cost of health care.
the evidence on the effect of tax expenditures on the cost and quality of health insurance is not conclusive.
the evidence is not yet sufficient for the conclusion that the tax treatment of employer-paid premiums has a significant impact on the demand for health care.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tax expenditures for health insurance are a major source of the inflationary pressures on the health care system and should be eliminated.

we have shown that the current system of health insurance in the U.S. is not only a major cause of the inflation in health care expenditures but is also an important source of inequity in the allocation of these expenditures.

we have shown that tax expenditures for employer-provided health insurance have been a major contributor to the increase in the cost of health care and have been a major factor in the increase in health care expenditures relative to the growth of the economy.

, if the goal is to increase enrollment in HMOs, then a better strategy is to reduce the tax subsidy on employer-paid health insurance premiums than to increase the out-of-pocket costs of individuals.
the federal government should be more transparent in how it uses tax policy to influence the provision of health insurance.
, while the tax subsidy is a powerful incentive to purchase insurance, it also encourages the purchase of insurance that is too generous.
